definitions.name: machine-slot-state
definitions.text: At one supported observation: a machine's slots in use are its active jobs (working); its other slots are idle. Read directly; nothing is derived.

definitions.name: flow-characterization-of-idle-slots
definitions.text: At one supported observation, for a machine with an idle slot: 'starved' when some unfinished unit still has a remaining routing step the published model makes this machine eligible for (a Queued unit's current step onward, an InProgress unit's later steps); otherwise 'no work left'. A Queued unit whose current step this machine serves while it has an idle slot is a contradiction under the current Engine and is rejected, not characterized.

definitions.name: utilization-over-a-period
definitions.text: For a machine and a period [a, b): the sum over ticks a..b-1 of its working slots at each tick's observation, divided by its slots times (b - a). Work in progress counts up to the period boundary; every machine is online throughout in these scenarios.

definitions.name: job-step-occurrences-from-supported-events
definitions.text: For the supported observation at a boundary, the supported events 1..latestEventSequence and the published model, with exactly one ORDER_ACCEPTED: number each accepted job by its position in ORDER_ACCEPTED.jobIds (unit 1 first). Pair every JOB_DISPATCHED with the event that made the job ready for that step (its previous JOB_STEP_COMPLETED, or ORDER_ACCEPTED for the first step) and with its own JOB_STEP_COMPLETED when one exists by the boundary; resolve the step through the accepted product's routing. A job that became ready for a step and has no dispatch for it by the boundary is an open wait. Refuse when any of those events was not retained, when other than one order was accepted, or when a dispatch or completion cannot be paired that way.

glossary.tick: One unit of simulated time. 'At tick 5' means the state right after everything that happens at tick 5.
glossary.step: One stage every loaf goes through: MIX, then BAKE, then PACK. Each step takes a fixed number of ticks.
glossary.machine: Something that does a step. A loaf is worked on by one machine at a time.
glossary.slot: Room on a machine for one loaf. Most machines have 1 slot; a 2-slot oven bakes two loaves at once.
glossary.loaf: One unit of the order. Loaves are numbered in the order they were released.
glossary.working: A slot is working while it holds a loaf: from the tick the loaf starts that step until the tick it finishes it.
glossary.idle: A slot is idle when it holds no loaf. Idle says nothing about why: see 'starved' and 'no work left'.
glossary.waiting: A loaf is waiting when it is ready for its next step but no machine has started it. Here a loaf never waits while a machine that can do its step is idle: work starts as soon as a slot is free.
glossary.starved: An idle machine is starved when work it will need is still upstream: some unfinished loaf will need this machine's step later, but none has reached it yet. It is decided from the whole bakery at that tick, not from the machine alone. Starved does NOT mean the machine is unnecessary, or that it is the problem: often a slower step before it sets the pace.
glossary.no work left: An idle machine has no work left when no unfinished loaf will ever need it again, or the order is done. Being idle at the end is not starvation.
glossary.blocked: In real factories a machine is blocked when it has finished an item but cannot pass it on, because the space after it is full. This bakery has unlimited space between steps, so nothing is ever blocked here. (A future concept.)
glossary.utilization: The share of a machine's available time spent working, over a stated period: working slot-ticks / (slots x ticks in the period). A 2-slot oven with one loaf for one tick is 50% for that tick. Always state the period: the same machine can be 70% over the whole run and 100% in the middle. The most utilized machine is NOT automatically the one to upgrade.
glossary.period: A stretch of ticks. 'From tick 4 to tick 14' covers ticks 4 up to 13: ten ticks. The whole run is from tick 0 to the tick the order finished.
glossary.variant: A pre-computed copy of a design with one change (or, where stated, two). Switch to it to inspect it; compare it to see how the finish time changed.
glossary.needed: A machine is needed if the order would finish later without it. One run cannot show that; removing the machine in a variant and comparing finish times can.
glossary.finish: The tick at which the last loaf of the order is packed.

scenarios.title: First bake
intro: Your bakery makes loaves. Every loaf goes through three steps: MIX, then BAKE, then PACK.
Here there is one machine per step, and an order of 4 loaves arrives all at once at tick 0.
Nothing is shown until you ask. Start with 'design', then try 'at 3' or 'machine Oven'.

scenarios.title: The big oven
intro: Same recipe, but the Oven now has 2 slots: it can bake two loaves at the same time.
The order is 6 loaves this time.

scenarios.title: Two upgrade options
intro: A slower recipe (MIX 2, BAKE 3, PACK 4 ticks) and an order of 8 loaves.
There are two versions of the bakery: version A has a second packer, version B a second oven.
You can switch between them and to pre-computed variants of each: type 'variants'.

designs.label: Version A without Packer 2
comparison: One change: removed Packer 2 (PACK). The order finished at tick 37 instead of 30 (7 ticks later).
This shows what happened with this change, not why.

designs.label: Version A + Mixer 2
comparison: One change: added Mixer 2 (MIX). The order finished at tick 30, the same as before.
This shows what happened with this change, not why.

designs.label: Version A + Oven 2
comparison: One change: added Oven 2 (BAKE). The order finished at tick 23 instead of 30 (7 ticks sooner).
This shows what happened with this change, not why.

designs.label: Version A + Packer 3
comparison: One change: added Packer 3 (PACK). The order finished at tick 30, the same as before.
This shows what happened with this change, not why.

designs.label: Version B without Oven 2
comparison: One change: removed Oven 2 (BAKE). The order finished at tick 37, the same as before.
This shows what happened with this change, not why.

designs.label: Version B + Mixer 2
comparison: One change: added Mixer 2 (MIX). The order finished at tick 37, the same as before.
This shows what happened with this change, not why.

designs.label: Version B + Oven 3
comparison: One change: added Oven 3 (BAKE). The order finished at tick 37, the same as before.
This shows what happened with this change, not why.

designs.label: Version B + Packer 2
comparison: One change: added Packer 2 (PACK). The order finished at tick 23 instead of 37 (14 ticks sooner).
This shows what happened with this change, not why.

scenarios.title: Two busy machines
intro: MIX 2, BAKE 4, PACK 4 ticks, one machine per step, and 8 loaves.
Pre-computed variants with extra machines are available: type 'variants'.

designs.label: + Mixer 2
comparison: One change: added Mixer 2 (MIX). The order finished at tick 38, the same as before.
This shows what happened with this change, not why.

designs.label: + Oven 2
comparison: One change: added Oven 2 (BAKE). The order finished at tick 38, the same as before.
This shows what happened with this change, not why.

designs.label: + Packer 2
comparison: One change: added Packer 2 (PACK). The order finished at tick 38, the same as before.
This shows what happened with this change, not why.

designs.label: + Oven 2 and Packer 2
comparison: 2 changes: added Oven 2 (BAKE); added Packer 2 (PACK). The order finished at tick 24 instead of 38 (14 ticks sooner).
This pair cannot tell how much each change contributed. Try them one at a time.

missions.prompt: Which machine is idle at tick 5?
missions.objective: Read a machine's state at a moment: working or idle.

parts.ask: Which machine is idle at tick 5?

missions.prompt: At tick 8 the Packer is idle. Why?
missions.objective: 'Starved': idle while work it will need is still upstream.

parts.ask: Is the Packer starved, or does it have no work left?

format.hint: Type: starved  or  no work left

missions.prompt: At tick 12 the Mixer is idle. Why?
missions.objective: Tell starvation apart from simply being finished.

parts.ask: Is the Mixer starved, or does it have no work left?

format.hint: Type: starved  or  no work left

missions.prompt: Which machine has the highest utilization over the whole run, and how much is it?
missions.objective: Utilization = time working / time available, over a stated period.

parts.ask: Which machine has the highest utilization over the whole run?
What is its utilization over the whole run?

format.hint: Type a percentage (e.g. 50%) or working ticks of available ticks (e.g. 8 of 16).

missions.prompt: Look at the Packer's idle time over the whole run.
missions.objective: An idle-time breakdown: a machine can be idle mostly because it is starved.

parts.ask: How many ticks was the Packer idle over the whole run?
Of those, how many ticks was it starved?

missions.prompt: At tick 9, how many of the Oven's 2 slots are working?
missions.objective: A machine can have several slots; state is per slot.

parts.ask: How many of the Oven's slots are working at tick 9?

missions.prompt: Look at the Oven's utilization over the whole run.
missions.objective: Per-slot utilization; idle slots at the start and the end lower it.

parts.ask: What is the Oven's utilization over the whole run?

format.hint: Type a percentage (e.g. 50%) or working ticks of available ticks (e.g. 8 of 16). Count slot-ticks: 2 slots for 1 tick = 2.

parts.ask: It is busy most of the time, so why is it not 100%?

missions.prompt: What is the Oven's utilization from tick 4 to tick 14?
missions.objective: The period changes the answer: always state the period.

parts.ask: What is the Oven's utilization from tick 4 to tick 14?

format.hint: Type a percentage (e.g. 50%) or working ticks of available ticks (e.g. 8 of 16).

missions.prompt: In version A, Packer 2 is idle at tick 13. Why?
missions.objective: Apply starvation in a design with two machines for one step.

parts.ask: Is Packer 2 starved, or does it have no work left?

format.hint: Type: starved  or  no work left

missions.prompt: Is Packer 2 needed, meaning the order would finish later without it?
missions.objective: 'Needed' is answered by an experiment (remove it and compare), not by looking at one run.

missions.prompt: In version B, Oven 2 is also idle and starved at times, just like Packer 2 in version A. Is Oven 2 needed?
missions.objective: Idle and starved look the same for a needed and an unneeded machine; only the experiment tells them apart.

missions.prompt: Which machine or machines have the highest utilization over the whole run?
missions.objective: Read utilization across machines; ties happen.

parts.ask: Which machine or machines have the highest utilization?

format.hint: Type one name, or several names separated by 'and'.

missions.prompt: Use the variants: where does added capacity make the order finish sooner?
missions.objective: High utilization does not tell you where added capacity helps; two steps can limit the order together.

parts.ask: Would adding a second oven make the order finish sooner?
Would adding a second packer make the order finish sooner?
Which change does make it finish sooner?

options: d) add an oven and a packer
